headline: Recommended City Council adopt zoning changes on parking, nonconforming structures, flood maps, street lists, and building codes.
summary: Members voted unanimously to recommend several zoning and building code amendments to the City Council. They also recommended that the Planning Board adopt site plan review changes. The meeting included updates on the 2050 Master Plan and Opportunity Zones 2.0.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the April 28, 2026 meeting unanimously.
Recommended that City Council adopt zoning amendments on parking, access, and loading, and that the Planning Board adopt site plan review amendments, unanimously.
Recommended that City Council adopt zoning amendments on nonconforming structures, unanimously.
Recommended that City Council adopt zoning overlay district map amendments, unanimously.
Recommended that City Council adopt amendments updating the list of arterial and collector streets, unanimously.
Recommended that City Council adopt building code amendments to Chapters 8, 26, and 27, unanimously.

1. Welcome by Chair and Comments by Mayor Champlin: Chair Gilboy welcomed those in 26

3. Regulatory Updates 35 
a) Zoning Amendments: Mr. Walsh provided a brief overview.  He discussed the 36 
City’s Council’s 2026/2027 City priorities and specifically Goal #2 under “Economic 37 
& Community Development” to “remove barriers to commercial and residential 38 
development through regulatory and administrative reform” and noted that the 39 
Community Development Department has prepared several zoning amendments over 40

Mr. Walsh explained that the latest batch of proposed amendments being presented to 8

amendments pertaining to FEMA Flood Insurance Rating Maps and roadway 10

i. Article 28-7 Access, Parking, Circulation and Loading and Site Plan 12 
Review Regulations Sections 18 (Parking Lot Design Standards), 19 13 
(Access and Driveway Standards), and 20 (Loading and Solid Waste 14 
Facility Standards): Tim Thompson provided a brief overview of these 15 
proposed amendments and associated staff report. It was noted that these 16 
amendments were particularly complicated to prepare due to linkages between 17 
the Zoning Ordinance and Site Plan Review Regulations.  Staff also noted that 18 
dozens of variations of the propose amendments had been prepared over the 19 
past 18 months before the final draft was ready for presentation to the City 20 
Council and Planning Board.  Mr. Thompson also noted that these 21 
amendments were a collaborative effort with multiple members of the 22 
Community Development Department.  He added that the proposed parking 23 
amendments have been a priority for City Administration, the development 24 
community, and Chamber of Commerce.  He provided an overview of the 25 
proposed amendments and provided a detail explanation of the interplay 26 
between the Zoning Ordinance and Site Plan Review regulations with respect 27 
to parking. It was noted that the proposed amendments will essentially 28 
eliminate the need for variances for standards associated with parking, loading 29 
and circulation, as flexibility will now be provided via Conditional Use 30 
Permits with the Planning Board and/or waivers to the site plan regulatory 31 
requirements as applicable (which are also within the Planning Board’s 32 
purview). 33 
 34 
A brief discussion ensued about changes to regulations pertaining to traffic 35 
medians. 36 
 37 
Mr. Walsh noted that the proposed amendments simplify and make the 38 
permitting process more efficient for staff and the development community, 39 
while protecting the public interest.  40

permit with the Planning Board rather than a special exception, thus giving the 50

Mr. Thompson also explained the purpose of proposed 28-8-7 and 28-8-8, 4 
which is intended to provide relief for subdivisions involving lawfully existing 5

regulations. As such, these amendments are proposed.   11

5. Opportunity Zones 2.0: Mr. Walsh provided a brief overview of the report included within 32 
the agenda packet. He explained that 53 census tracts in New Hampshire qualify for potential 33 
inclusion in the program, including two in Concord.  However, of the 53 eligible tracts, the 34 
State can only select 25 tracts for inclusion in the program per Federal regulations.  The State 35 
is currently accepting applications for nominations, and the City will nominate the two tracts 36 
in Concord by the August 28th deadline.  Development projects in those tracts enrolled in the 37 
Opportunity Zone 2.0 Program will be eligible to receive special federal tax incentives.  38
